Nia (AE): Orion Systems emailed — they want a short POC to replace CompetitorX. Goals: keep client changes minimal (drop-in bridge), quantify token billing delta, and finish their security appendix. Can we scope owners and blockers?
Owen (SE): Sounds fine. First question: do they require exact streaming frame compatibility or just equivalent semantics? That will decide adapter complexity.
Nia (AE): They said "no client changes if possible" and specifically called out streaming frames and webhook callbacks as brittle.
Faye (Solutions): We can implement a small bridge that speaks CompetitorX framing on the front and calls Redwood behind the scenes. I'll draft a mapping doc for frames, headers, and tool payloads.
Owen (SE): Streaming nuance: CompetitorX emits incremental frames named "delta" with seq numbers and occasionally a "meta:tool" frame. Our runtime emits token streams. Bridge should rewrap our chunks into their "delta" frames and surface tool outputs as the same "meta:tool" event.
Marco (Infra): POC infra ask: they expect p99 < 230ms for short completions. Recommend a dedicated eu-central pool for the test to remove cross-region variance. I can provision nodes once scope is firm.
Ruth (Security): Questionnaire highlights: EU-only residency, CMK option, SOC2 coverage, IP allowlist, SSO/SCIM, and a clause that fallback cannot forward raw prompts. They want the appendix by Friday.
Nia (AE): Legal also asked for a clear description of what happens during automatic fallback — specifically whether any user prompt or full response could be routed to CompetitorX.
Ruth (Security): We'll provide an attestation: automatic fallback uses only minimal routing metadata and does not forward full request/response bodies. We'll also offer a config to disable fallback for the POC. I'll prepare exact wording.
Faye (Solutions): For billing parity I propose running a token reconciliation across their sample corpus. Example command I'll run: 
python tools/token_reconcile.py --source competitorx-v1 --target redwood-2026 --input orion_samples.jsonl --out orion_token_deltas.csv
Faye (Solutions): That will give per-request token diffs and a net delta we can multiply by their monthly volume to produce a cost comparison. I'll include a short README about tokenization edge cases (special separators, trailing whitespace).
Owen (SE): We should also compute response variance metrics: exact-match rate, normalized edit distance, and embedding cosine for the top result. Target threshold: >= 82% semantic similarity on 250 core prompts for initial acceptance. I'll build a small eval harness (docker) they can run locally.
Marco (Infra): Canary plan I suggest: 1) bridge deployed in staging (no traffic), 2) dedicated pool + latency smoke, 3) 5% canary with immediate rollback triggers (error rate, latency, semantic regression). I'll add tracing tags to identify POC flows.
Nia (AE): Orion asked for a demo in 6 business days. Can the team deliver?
Owen (SE): Prototype the bridge and streaming frame mapper today; should have a working demo endpoint in 3 days if we limit scope to /v1/generate.
Faye (Solutions): I'll run the token reconciliation and start the eval harness runs tonight. Will push results to the POC repo.
Ruth (Security): Appendix answers and fallback attestation by Fri EOD.
kickoff-bot: infra: staging-orion created, 2 GPUs reserved, logging stream enabled.
Marco (Infra): I can standby for provisioning once Faye shares the final scope + sample corpus.
Nia (AE): I'll ask Orion for the corpus and a short header list their client depends on. Scheduling a 20-min kickoff for tomorrow. Thanks all :pray:
